entities.name: Abel Gabuza
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abel Gabuza (born 1949) is a South African Catholic prelate who served as Coadjutor Archbishop of Durban, making him one of the most senior African Catholic leaders in South Africa. Born in the Eastern Cape during the apartheid era, he was ordained a priest and rose through the South African Catholic hierarchy to become a coadjutor archbishop in one of the country's largest archdioceses.

Gabuza's career spans the final decades of apartheid and the entire post-apartheid period. The Catholic Church in South Africa was a significant institutional voice against apartheid — through the Southern African Catholic Bishops' Conference (SACBC) and through individual bishops — and Black African clergy like Gabuza embodied the transition to indigenous Catholic leadership that was both theologically necessary and politically symbolic in the post-apartheid context.

Durban's archdiocese serves one of South Africa's most ethnically diverse Catholic communities, including large Zulu, Indian, coloured, and white populations. Gabuza's appointment as coadjutor represented the transition to majority Black African leadership in an archdiocese that had long been led by European missionaries. His ministry engaged the social challenges of post-apartheid South Africa — inequality, HIV/AIDS, crime, and the continuing legacy of racial dispossession.
